slides.1.title: Level 3 key points
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Sake
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Koji turns starch into sugar; multiple parallel fermentation, about 15–16%; kimoto and yamahai rely on natural lactic bacteria; honjozo 70, ginjo 60, daiginjo 50; junmai has no added alcohol; namazake is unpasteurised
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Serving sake
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Ginjo chilled for aroma, junmai and yamahai can be warmed; positive SMV leans drier; umami and low acidity suit seafood and sushi
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Beer
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Ale top-fermented and warmer, lager bottom-fermented and cool; Pilsner 1842 in Plzeň; stout from roasted barley; Hefeweizen banana and clove; lambic spontaneous; lager about 3–7°C
slides.1.content: CMS orals cross categories: answer in the order raw material → process → style → service.
